title: I Printed the Little-Free-Pantry Restock After They Dumped Expired Cans

parts.text: I opened the box at 8:07 a.m. and neighbor Cal had stacked dented cans dated last March. The card said: IN-DATE ONLY. LABEL THE DATE. NO DUMPING. I was thirty-six, steward, holding a restock sheet. Cal shrugged. "Neighbors are the pantry." I photographed the dates, the card, and the stack. Then I asked for the restock log. At 8:14 the mutual-aid lead pinged why Cal's name was on expired stock. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The mutual-aid lead can see Cal's March dates on the restock log.

social.video_title: They dumped March cans into the little free pantry — Part 1/2
social.description: Community pantry, expired dates, a steward sheet. I logged the dump. Would you have photographed the stack?

parts.text: Cal called it sharing until the lead asked for the still. I printed the log, the card, and the photo. The March cans left in a labeled bag. Cal restocked in-date and told the next neighbor sharing was always about optics. Optics is a word dumpers use when a card exists. Restock now has a second line: DATES ARE THE PANTRY. I keep the sheet. Cal brown-bags his jokes. The box finally looks like food, not a chute. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Restock log, bagged cans, and a second line. Was sharing ever March?
